hints: Take half of the coefficient of $x$ (which is $3$) and form $(x+3)^2$.
walkthrough:
Complete the square for the quadratic expression $x^2 + 6x + 2$:
$$x^2 + 6x + 2 = (x + 3)^2 - 3^2 + 2$$

Simplify the constant terms to obtain the completed square form:
$$(x + 3)^2 - 9 + 2 = (x + 3)^2 - 7$$

hints: Solve $|x+3| > 4$ by considering the two regions $x+3 > 4$ and $x+3 < -4$.
walkthrough:
Set up the inequality and use the completed square form from part (i):
$$(x + 3)^2 - 7 > 9 \implies (x + 3)^2 > 16$$

Take the square root of both sides to establish the two linear inequalities:
$$x + 3 > 4 \quad\text{or}\quad x + 3 < -4$$

Solve each inequality for $x$ to state the solution set:
$$x > 1 \quad\text{or}\quad x < -7$$
